author: @TheManCybo
text: There's a big problem with time. It doesn't exist, it's a human construct to make it easier comprehend our memories. A clock, atomic or mechanical isn't a prove time exist. About relativity where fast moving objects are slower in time, measured with a clock, it can be explained: For this to work, the speed of the moving object must be very high. In experiments with satellites which have atomic clocks synchronized with the same ones on earth, they showed to be slower for a few seconds in a period of an year. The measurement of the clocks are no prove time exist, it proves only a difference between the two of them. Why? Gravity and speed. All objects moving with high speed are getting inert. But earths gravity is pulling the material structure of the clock on the satellite while it's traveling ca. 20 km per second. this is what slowing material down. This applies also for very high speed, linear traveling trough the universe, gravity is everywhere. Ever rotating on a playground on those round platforms with handles? With enough speed you couldn't even move your hand to the center of the platform - the kinetic energy of the spinning is pulling you away from the center, so material is getting inert, lazy. The satellite is also spinning around earth, plus the gravity of it: 2 forces - centrifugal and gravity pulling from earth. Imagine how it works with stars and galaxies. But time doesn't exist. If time would exist, science would find a way to catch it, to establish a timeline. Imagine our present moment makes a never ending imprint in something like timeline, of course, no future yet - it simply didn't happened yet. So, science must be able to enter this timeline at any past point in it, like with a time machine. But if it would be possible, they would jump in a point of the timeline which is frozen till the moment they jump in. At this point, they should move forward in the timeline. It's practically in every movie. Does this means, all past timeline is frozen, until time travelers enter? Or is every moment (what is a moment, how long is it?) in constant loop? The problem with this movie is, mankind could never get to the future without installing the wormhole. The wormhole is allegedly the reason that mankind exist in the future. So, for mankind to get to its future, it would have to preinstall the wormhole in the present to get to the future. One could say, they got away from earth with the missing data about anti gravity and got to the 3 planets. Still, how could they install the wormhole to get to those planets, since the future is established only with the existing of the wormhole? There is simply now way to get to future without setting the wormhole in the present. And this couldn't be done by humanity, this future never happened.

author: @pauldh62
text: This is a compelling and perplexing film that I never tire of watching. Part of my problem is that I have only ever seen it on long haul flights to Kenya and the sound quality isn't brilliant. On the one hand I never cease to well up when Cooper has to leave his daughter and the real strength is that love transcends all which is great. On the other, he meets his daughter for barely three minutes after a separation of most of her lifetime, leaves with that love intact and blithely swans off to pursue an unconvincing romantic attachment somewhere in the galaxy. While much of the film seems to pride itself on observing scientific theory, particularly physics within the confines of this universe, it goes out on a leap, using a convenient worm hole and has the heroes explore rather uninteresting worlds in a doomed galaxy - it's orbiting a blackhole, so game over, plus Cooper goes hurtling into this unchartered anomaly to emerge unscathed and does not become the crushed spaghetti one is believed to become if one was ever able to effect so suicidal a manoeuvre. In addition, just what was the answer to overcoming the question they were searching for? My understanding was that there was no answer, so when this revelation occurred it made no sense.

author: @Mystikan
text: The idea I got from the scenes inside the black hole is this: when you pass the event horizon, all paths lead to the singularity. At no point is it possible to get further away from the singularity, or even to remain at a constant distance from it. This means that the dimension of space in the direction of the singularity becomes timelike, so time as experienced outside the black hole must become spacelike. This means that he can move back and forth through time in the same manner he normally could through a given dimension of space - at least for as long as he has before he becomes spaghettified by proximity to the singularity, which is his inescapable future. So the "library" inside the black hole to me represented universal time as a spacelike dimension in which he could move at will, because his formerly spacelike path to the singularity had become his axis of time. This is what enabled him to travel back in time to his daughter's childhood and leave the message "STAY" on her bookshelf before he was crushed by the singularity.

author: @mariusgirbo8614
text: While I admire your channel and videos I think this time you are trying to find meanings that are simply not there. The ending is fantastic indeed, like the rest of the movie for that matter, however the meaning of it is pretty clear and makes perfect sense if you don't want to get emotional and add love into the mix or 'what happens after we die' scenarios. The Tesseract was build and put there together with the wormhole, by the humans from the future. Not the near future, but a very distant one, where humans evolved into a specie that is no longer bend by time. That is why they didn't put it there themselves. Brand briefly explains this concept when they are stuck on the water planet. The Tesseract's single purpose is to offer Cooper a way to communicate the equations from inside the black hole out to the real world (Murph in this case) so the humanity can save itself. As current physics states that in theory nothing can come out from a black hole, we can assume that the advanced human specie from the future had the technology to do this and the Tesseract was the hardware to do it. The way this is done - extraordinary vision from Nolan and the crew - is through gravity. Why Gravity? Because Gravity is the only one of the four fundamental forces of the universe that the current physics cannot explain. Yes, real cause of gravity is unknown for science at this moment, we only know how it works and it's effects. So with gravity unsolved even for real science, it is a genius use of it in the movie script. The 'Cooper station' where he wakes up, which you are calling 'A conical station with an opening at the end allowing sun light to filter in.. Light at the end of the tunnel? - this literally made me smile (no offense please, but it did :) ) - no, this is a O’neill cylinder, a very common and well known term in the sci-fi field describing potential habitable structure in space. You can find the O’neill cylinders both in sci-fi literature since 1950 but also in the current science theories about living in space. You can find very much material about O’neill cylinders on Google. And finally the Tesseract was not build by love. The love they talk about during the movie is the reason why Cooper thinks his daughter will come back to her home (and eventually find the watch). Because she loves him. Cooper actually tells this to TAR the robot while they are trapped inside the Tesseract. Love is also brought into discussion few more times during the movie, with various attributes like 'not time or space dependent', but this is more of a philosophical subject and adds to the overall movie quality. However, love did not create the Tesseract. Nevertheless, a brilliant movie. A perfect combination of real, well documented science mixed with great speculation and imagination regarding the unknown science. Keep up the good work, as said above I love your channel.

text: The physics is totally f***ed up in the movie. Yes, time goes slower in gravitational field. But the authors do not realize just HOW STRONG the field has to be for time to be slowed that much. The planet has to be barely above innermost stable orbit around black hole - and it means that to land on it, the spacecraft has to go down almost all the way deep into lowest orbits around black hole to reach the planet, land on it, then launch from it AGAIN, and then climb back out of the black hole gravity well. I'd say they need a delta-V of about 100000 km/s to do all that. Remember, in reality, just the step of launching from an earth-like planet to low orbit around it, takes ~9 km/s of delta-V. And they do it all on a shuttle barely the size of a truck. STUPID.

author: @defiant4eva
text: I like Nolan's films, outside of the dark knight rises and man of steel. As he is not afraid to leave a film with the right questions, instead of the "wait, what?" questions. Interstellar like Momento, the prestige and Inception ask you to question yourself, your culture and political views without pushing one side of the narrative. Plus they also challenge the viewer to keep up and don't spoon feed them clues or answers. Interstellar starts off in a world where the eco-system is failing and doesn't have some narrator or news media montage explaining this. he treats his audience as if they have a brain and leaves enough clues or dialogue in the film for the audience to work it out or at least understand and accept it. You know, unlike so many directors. Actor A says "Grab that spoon", to actor B, the camera then zooms in on a spoon on the table. Actor B walks over and grabs the spoon and says "I got the spoon" Camera zooms in on their hand with the spoon. or you know this old trick. Actor A says to the group of people "We are safe now" Camera pans away from the group and zooms into a dark corner of the room, usually a sound of scratching or cracking starts. Or a visual clue of a drain opening or something. Mainly used in shitty horror films, you know the type of film where the characters kill off the main villain/evil/monster only for it to reappear moments later for round 2-3 or 4.

author: @stephenmata1821
text: When I watched this film, I noticed the contrast between the twelve explorers sent out with no personal attachments, and Cooper, whose deep attachment to his children drove his every choice. The parallel to our own society is striking: those who set out to “save humanity” in the abstract may justify sacrificing countless lives for their vision, while those motivated by love for their families often create the most powerful ripple effects that truly preserve society. Paradoxically, pursuing what seems selfless can lead to cold detachment and selfish outcomes, while pursuing the good of one’s own family can become the truest form of selflessness.

author: @___P___H___T___M___
text: Interstellar feels like a direct allegory to my life after I turned 21. I lived in Phoenix making dogshit money, feeding off scraps, toiling in the Arizona heat fixing old supercars. I dreamt of leaving and heading to a whole new part of the world. I finally made it happen and moved all the way to Australia with the hope of building a better life and potentially bringing my girlfriend and parents over there to live with me once everything was settled. Little did I know - this continent would be like nowhere else on this planet. Its a strange mirrored image of America but with deadly beautiful creatures, ancient flora, and dazzling displays of nature in its most unfiltered form. Chaos and uncertainty were the only guaranteed constant as days turned to weeks, and weeks to months, and months to years in a massive blur. Back at home, my family and friends missed me to the point of agony. Some even cut ties with me because they were convinced they would never see me again. As the years went by, the hope of bringing my loved ones over here faded into oblivion, and I began to realise how much I was missing out on. Birthdays, weddings, promotions, arrivals of children, the loss of my soulmate, all happening at home while I may aswell have been on another planet. My friends and family began to noticeably age with the times, and like Cooper watching the video messages, I felt I had missed everything while I stayed exactly the same - and I began to break down. I realised I was on a path that was truly mine, and mine alone. The characters in Interstellar represent the different facets of my ego. Cooper is my will, Brand is my hope, Romilly is my curiosity, TARS is my charisma, CASE is my anxiety, Mann is my fear, and Murphy is my heart. In my manic wanderlust and unshakable urge for adventure - I brought everything with me but my heart. I left behind everything that mattered in my life as a sacrifice for a better future in a new world. Now I'm 30 - still building. Still setting up camp for a family that may never come. My friends have their own homes, families and careers now. My parents have grown old and they struggle with travelling these days. Everyone still asks me to come home, to be with the people who love me, to pick up where we all left off and try to make up for the time we lost. I would love nothing more than to oblige them. But something about this place - this otherwordly continent - makes me want to keep pressing on. Something in my future wants me to S-T-A-Y

author: @thesharpercoder
text: Interesting video. The best part was the return of the classic closing credits. The 5th dimension is purely speculative. I would categorize it with dark matter and dark energy. They are something we made to explain something we do not yet understand. Have you ever heard of the “Arrow of Time”? The Universe as we know is comprised of Space-Time, which is three dimensions of Space and one dimension of Time. The Arrow of Time moves us relentlessly forward. More about that in a moment. Mathematicians have been able to better understand what occurs inside the event horizon of a black hole. Time and Space swap places inside of an event horizon. Instead of Space-Time, you now have Time-Space. The math supports the concept of three dimensions of Time and one dimension of Space. Instead of an Arrow of Time, there exists and Arrow of Space, which relentlessly moves you toward a singularity. This is what being “spaghettified” means! If the Arrow of Space inside an event horizon moves you toward a singularity, then what does that say about the Arrow of Time outside an event horizon? Are we moving toward a singularity? No, the reality is the exact opposite. The Arrow of Time is moving us away from a singularity. The singularity has a familiar name, The Big Bang.

Due to the immense tidal forces from the black hole, the planet is prolated/distorted in a direction that is alligned with the black hole relative to the planet. The tidal bores are caused by a rocking of the planet in combination with the prolation/distortion, which the physics/maths works out to be an hour per wave, plus the waves are huge in that case.

text: You explained it well, but it still has a plot hole as big as Back to the Future 2. If the future "earthlings" were advanced enough to place a worm hole for Cooper, that means humanity never went extinct. They escaped earth WITHOUT needing the worm hole, so why did they even put it there? Unless they are alien, in which case it is never explained what their motivation is for helping earth survive. And why not just fly into earth and rescue everyone and help them build space colonies? That's actually more feasible than a worm hole. Then in BTTF2, it's impossible to travel into the future and see yourself and your kids because you would have skipped over 30 years of time where you seemingly disappeared, just as Einstein disappeared for 1 minute in BTTF1. So Marty would not exist for 30 years, no life, no kids. Time travel movies are very difficult to pull off without breaking logic.

text: Definitely a subscriber. Despite the negative comments, I found that your video had a interesting idea for the outcome and interpretation of the movie. For me, I interpret the ending that these were not advanced humans millions of years into the future, that created the wormhole etc. I say this because if the population starting on Edmunds planet (with Brand starting the surrogacy) was so far evolved past our current species and created a wormhole and "tesseract," then it would create a paradox. I believe it's called the Bootstrap paradox? A good example of this paradox is if you were at home and received a book called "how to build a time machine" and built it over the course of 10 years or so..... You would wonder, "who could have sent me this book?" Then it dawns on you that, "hey, it was me! I could send myself and this book back in time, ten years to my younger self!" Paradox! You could only build the time machine if you discovered the book but you can only discover the book if you made the time machine.... it would be as if nobody has discovered the book or time machine and it would be stuck in this form of causal loop. Both of them cannot exist without the other. This is why I believe that instead of humans, it was a different form of advanced life. This still creates some issues with TARS attempting to relay the quantum data when he/she/it was inside the tesseract. It caused anomalies with Cooper's Ranger (causing a crash years ago in Earth-time), etc. Another plausible idea is having multiple or an infinite number of what we perceive as a universe. Example: you may have created a time machine with your own free will and sent the book back in time but instead you "traveled" into a different universe altogether, changing their version of time. Maybe time just doesn't exist? Maybe it's possible that everything that exists always had a past, present and future that was already set. Time is relative....we feel the present, remember the past and dream about the future.

author: @revparravager
text: While seemingly complex, the ending of Interstellar always struck me as actually VERY simple to explain. The fact that the protagonist actually TELLS you precisely what is happening is the key. The fact that a species who has evolved beyond the normal limitations of Space-Time and is trying to communicate with a Human is the explanation. Its all a matter of perspective and in order to achieve a state of control within a 3 dimensional frame of reference that he could understand required them to forcibly "simplify" it to ensure that he can understand. This is precisely why (and its even explained by he himself) they limited his "interface" with them to a very small 3 dimensional set of coordinates but extrapolated over the duration of time. Now admittedly this is where the movie goes off the rails a bit because it has fallen into an "oversimplification trap" as it regards Time which is often the error in any movie in which Time is being manipulated, traversed or made flexible. Time is NOT, I repeat NOT, a "dimension" let alone a "4th dimension". Dimensions are STRICTLY defined by physical parameters and what has to be understood is that Time is a component of that Space that is intrinsically linked. Space and Time (or more accurately Spacetime because they cannot be separated) are bound inextricably and while they do function mathematically as a 4 dimensional manifold its less about actual dimensionality and more about a dimension in the sense of just another variable to be considered in what would otherwise be a strictly x, y, z system. In the case of this movie the species which is communicating with him (or rather allow HIM to communicate with his daughter using their technology) is able to traverse "time" because he is manipulating Gravity. Its already known that Gravity and its influence on Time is very well defined. For example, the best know relationship is such that at faster velocities (and thus greater and greater Gravity) time literally slows down within that frame of reference as it relates to other frames of reference. The fact that everyone has heard the very basic example of "as you travel near the speed of light time appears to stop for the traveler but only from outside their reference as observed by someone NOT travelling at the speed of light" but the correlary to this situation is that to the person who is moving at light speed the outside universe would appear to be on "Fast Forward" compared to them. The ONLY reason this occurs is NOT because you are traveling fast its because by doing so you are also increasing the force of gravity and thus warping the flow of time because you literally gain Mass the faster you go. More Mass, more Gravity. More Gravity, Slower Time. At the core of a Black Hole for instance you would have the unenviable experience to be being pulled apart at the atomic level and also stretched for what would essentially be the end of the Universe. THESE Beings (whether they are really Us or just Helpful Aliens, it doesn't matter) allow him to manipulate Gravity to allow him to communicate by figuring it out within his own context. They are limited in their interactions with him because it would be like having a Human try to communicate and empower a 2-dimensional "flat" lifeform to exist within an infinite number of planes that extend along Time. Now admittedly this is where the movie goes off the rails a bit because it has fallen into an "oversimplification trap" as it regards Time which is often the error in any movie in which Time is being manipulated, traversed or made flexible. Time is NOT, I repeat NOT, a "dimension" let alone a "4th dimension". Dimensions are STRICTLY defined by physical parameters and what has to be understood is that Time is a component of that Space that is intrinsically linked. Space and Time (or more accurately Spacetime because they cannot be separated) are bound inextricably and while they do function maththematically as a 4 dimensional manifold its less about actual dimensionality and more about a dimension in the sense of just another variable to be considered in what would otherwise be a strictly x, why, z systthem. The fact that everyone has heard the very basic example of "as you travel near the speed of light time appears to stop for the traveler but only from outside their reference as observed by someone NOT travelling at the speed of light" but the correlary to this situation is that to the person who is moving at light speed the outside universe would appear to be on "Fast Forward" compared to ththem. author: @vids290
text: I was growing magic mushrooms and travelling to the furthest regions of my mind when i came across interstellar. The insights and information i was bringing back felt so important but having a daughter under 5 and another baby daughter watching the film scared the hell out of me. I made a decision to stop travelling and stay grounded with my wife and daughters, that was about 7 years ago but i definitely made the right choice. What scared me the most was goin too far and missing my daughter's lives, the scene where Murph is on her death bed haunted me...turned out to be a really important movie in my life and will probably always hold a special place in my heart.
